[c0]
### Steps to reproduce

<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
  # If you want to test against edge Rails replace the previous line with this:
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"

  gem "sqlite3"
end

require "active_record/railtie"
require "minitest/autorun"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = "sqlite3::memory:"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f
  config.eager_load = false
  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

  config.active_record.encryption.primary_key = "primary_key"
  config.active_record.encryption.deterministic_key = "deterministic_key"
  config.active_record.encryption.key_derivation_salt = "key_derivation_salt"
end
Rails.application.initialize!

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.string :encrypted_working
    t.string :encrypted_compressed
    t.string :encrypted_custom_compressor
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  encrypts :encrypted_working
  encrypts :encrypted_compressed, compress: false
  encrypts :encrypted_custom_compressor, compressor: ->(value) { value.reverse }
end

module CustomCompressor
  def self.deflate(data)
    data
  end

  def self.inflate(data)
    data
  end
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_encrypted_working
    post = ActiveRecord::Encryption.without_encryption do
      Post.create!(encrypted_working: "hello")
    end

    refute post.encrypted_attribute?(:title)
  end

  def test_compress_false
    post = ActiveRecord::Encryption.without_encryption do
      Post.create!(encrypted_compressed: "hello")
    end

    refute post.encrypted_attribute?(:encrypted_compressed)
  end

  def test_custom_compressor
    post = ActiveRecord::Encryption.without_encryption do
      Post.create!(encrypted_custom_compressor: "hello")
    end

    refute post.encrypted_attribute?(:encrypted_custom_compressor)
  end
end
```

To replicate the issue in `active_record`'s tests you can modify [`PostEncrypted` line 13](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/test/models/post_encrypted.rb#L13) to `encrypts :title, compress: false` and you will see that `bundle exec rake test:sqlite3_mem TEST=/workspaces/rails/activerecord/test/cases/encryption/contexts_test.rb` also fails.

### Expected behavior

Even when the `compress: false` or `compressor: <custom_compressor>` options are passed  the encryption context should be honored - in the case of the test above `without_encryption` the `NullEncryptor` should be used.

### Actual behavior

The encryption context (specifically, the encryptor) is being overridden when `compress: false` or `compressor: <custom compressor>` options are passed to `encrypts`

I believe the bug stems from the fact that the encryptor is being [overridden in the scheme](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/lib/active_record/encryption/scheme.rb#L32-L33).

### System configuration

**Rails version**: `8.0.2`

**Ruby version**: `3.4.2`

title: 8.0.2 breaks secret_key_base in development
need_summary: The developer wanted to know if the change to secret_key_base handling in Rails 8.0.2 was a security issue, and the answer cites commit 0c76f17f2dbf0d7ad90c890e6f334743cacce41f and PR #53705 confirming the behavior is fixed and correct in 8.0.2.
security_topic: breaking change in secret_key_base handling in Rails 8.0.2
question_text: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 introduces a breaking change to those who use a single `config/credentials.yml.enc` file and rely on the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file in development to provide `secret_key_base`. With 8.0.2 `secret_key_base` will always be read from `config/credentials.yml.enc` regardless of environment. The obvious symptoms will be invalid sessions and broken attachments in Action Text.
answer_text: That was a bug. If you look the code that I removed https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0c76f17f2dbf0d7ad90c890e6f334743cacce41f, the idea is that `credentials.secret_key_base` always took precedence over the temporary file. In that commit I broke that behavior. And in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 the behavior is fixed. 8.0.2 has the right behavior.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54778: 8.0.2 breaks secret_key_base in development
Author: brendon
Date: 2025-03-18T19:51:34Z
Labels: With reproduction steps
State: closed

[c0]
https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 introduces a breaking change to those who use a single `config/credentials.yml.enc` file and rely on the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file in development to provide `secret_key_base`. With 8.0.2 `secret_key_base` will always be read from `config/credentials.yml.enc` regardless of environment. The obvious symptoms will be invalid sessions and broken attachments in Action Text.

In 8.0.1 and in all previous Rails versions (except 7.1 at some point) the default behaviour was to load `secret_key_base` from the tmp file in development and test and load it from the encrypted secrets in production.

I have proposed a PR to reverse https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 with some enhancement allowed for loading the `secret_key_base` from the environment specific credentials file if it exists. This allows existing apps to keep working and provides a migration path for those that want to use the per-environment credentials files going forward:

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54554

I'm not opposed to a more robust credentials system not reliant on a flimsy tmp file but https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 is a breaking change that should have been more clearly signalled and should not have occurred in a patch release.

For history:

- The introduction of encrypted credentials: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/30067
- The introduction of per-environment credentials: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/33521

[c1] @brendon 2025-03-18T20:01:49Z:
For extra clarity. The breaking change was introduced based on this issue: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54277#issue-2794696317

It was a user that started their app on 7.1 and so had the "broken" behaviour to begin with and was then confused when this was reverted back to what it originally was.

The 7.1 break in behaviour may have been precipitated by the removal of `Rails.application.secrets`.

comments.author: brendon
comments.body:
https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 introduces a breaking change to those who use a single `config/credentials.yml.enc` file and rely on the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file in development to provide `secret_key_base`. With 8.0.2 `secret_key_base` will always be read from `config/credentials.yml.enc` regardless of environment. The obvious symptoms will be invalid sessions and broken attachments in Action Text.

In 8.0.1 and in all previous Rails versions (except 7.1 at some point) the default behaviour was to load `secret_key_base` from the tmp file in development and test and load it from the encrypted secrets in production.

I have proposed a PR to reverse https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 with some enhancement allowed for loading the `secret_key_base` from the environment specific credentials file if it exists. This allows existing apps to keep working and provides a migration path for those that want to use the per-environment credentials files going forward:

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54554

I'm not opposed to a more robust credentials system not reliant on a flimsy tmp file but https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53705 is a breaking change that should have been more clearly signalled and should not have occurred in a patch release.

For history:

- The introduction of encrypted credentials: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/30067
- The introduction of per-environment credentials: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/33521

need_summary: The developer asked if a default gitignore entry for *.key files could be added to prevent credential leaks, and the maintainer answered with a concrete PR reference (https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54774) that implements the change.
security_topic: preventing accidental credential exposure via gitignore
question_text: All of this could have been avoided by just adding a default gitignore config/credentials/*.key. Would it be possible to add it to the default gitignore, or maybe when generating a new env?
answer_text: This is a great suggestion. I opened a PR for it: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54774
thread_text:
DISCUSSION #54773: Gitignoring all *.key files
Author: lethaale
Date: 2025-03-17T12:27:46Z

[c0]
Hello!

We just had a small security accident where a .key file has been exposed that could have been prevented with a broader config/credentials/*.key gitignore.

**Context**
In a project we have 3 different environments, for internal reasons that make sense we are not using development staging and production, but production and, for simplicity, E1
we needed to replace E1 with E2, possibly without changing all the API keys
One of the devs did all the credentials correctly, but he didn't catch that in the gitignore e1.key was gitignored, and when renaming to e2.key to test that it was actually working, he pushed it to github opening a PR. 
Key is now burnt, we have to rotate all the credentials in all the third parties. 

Not a big deal from a security pov because it's an internal testing env, but if this happened in prod we would be in a war room.

All of this could have been avoided by just adding a default gitignore config/credentials/*.key. Would it be possible to add it to the default gitignore, or maybe when generating a new env?

EDIT: I know that when creating a new key it gets added to the gitignore, but only that key. The problem was the renaming

Thanks a lot in advance 🤟🏿

title: ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError with bidirectional foreign key
need_summary: The developer asked if they could safely modify an ActiveStorage blob’s key to include the user ID, and the maintainer answered that the key is a secure token generated automatically and must not be changed, citing the ActiveStorage::Blob key implementation and documentation.
security_topic: modifying ActiveStorage blob key security implications
question_text: The original intent of modifying the `key` was because I would like to have my files in the remote storage (i.e. Amazon S3) to be easily findable and also contains the information of the `user.id`. And I'm quite not sure if there are any other ways of achieving that intent.
answer_text:
I don't think this has anything special to do with your associations, but modifying the `key` directly like this is not supported.

The key is a secure token designed to be unique and generated automatically:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/ce359806416550c3b1b790c116aee5f0f9a182d4/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L22

See also: https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveStorage/Blob.html#method-i-key

> The key is the secure-token format from Rails in lower case. So it’ll look like: xtapjjcjiudrlk3tmwyjgpuobabd. This key is not intended to be revealed directly to the user. Always refer to blobs using the [signed_id](https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveStorage/Blob.html#method-i-signed_id) or a verified form of the key.

And: https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveStorage/Blob.html

> Blobs are intended to be immutable in as-so-far as their reference to a specific file goes. You’re allowed to update a blob’s metadata on a subsequent pass, but you should not update the key or change the uploaded file. If you need to create a derivative or otherwise change the blob, simply create a new blob and purge the old one.

Does this match your understanding or am I missing something?

title: Strong parameters allow unpermitted parameters when merging a hash
need_summary: Whether merging a hash into ActionController::Parameters can unintentionally mark nested parameters as permitted, potentially bypassing strong‑parameter protection, with the explanation and proposed changes documented in Rails PR #52997 and PR #54837.
security_topic: permitted status inheritance in parameter merging
question_text: location should have been merged as non-permitted
answer_text:
This is the expected behavior, as `merge` will return a _new instance_ with the inherited permitted status (i.e. `permitted` is sticky).

It seems difficult to change this expectation, albeit dangerous, so perhaps updating the documentation is our best path forward.

You should not use `permit` until you're done mutating the parameters.

```ruby
params = ActionController::Parameters.new(name: "Buddy")
new_params = params.merge(age: 42)

pp new_params
#=> #<ActionController::Parameters {"name" => "Buddy", "age" => 42} permitted: false>

pp new_params.permit(:name, :age).to_h
#=> {"name" => "Buddy", "age" => 42}
```

### Expected behavior
`location` should have been merged as non-permitted
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->

### Actual behavior
`location` is considered permitted unless you access it, which makes it be casted to an unpermitted param
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->

### System configuration

**Ruby version**: 3.0.5

[c1] @zzak 2025-03-13T00:44:29Z:
This is the expected behavior, as `merge` will return a _new instance_ with the inherited permitted status (i.e. `permitted` is sticky).

It seems difficult to change this expectation, albeit dangerous, so perhaps updating the documentation is our best path forward.

You should not use `permit` until you're done mutating the parameters.

```ruby
params = ActionController::Parameters.new(name: "Buddy")
new_params = params.merge(age: 42)

pp new_params
#=> #<ActionController::Parameters {"name" => "Buddy", "age" => 42} permitted: false>

pp new_params.permit(:name, :age).to_h
#=> {"name" => "Buddy", "age" => 42}
```

title: Race condition in with_routing integration test helper
need_summary: The problem is that Rails' with_routing resets Devise's warden failure_app, causing authentication failures, and it is fixed in Devise PR #5728 (see https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/pull/5728) and further addressed in PR #5769.
security_topic: warden failure app reset causing authentication failure in tests
question_text: I still havent' figured out what's resetting the `warden_config` when `with_routing` block gets executed.
answer_text:
Thanks for the reproduction script! It's indeed a problem in devise that started since Rails 7.2

I submitted a PR to fix this upstream: https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/pull/5769 Hopefully it will get accepted.

I'll close this issue since there is not much to do in Rails.

Author: quixoten
Date: 2025-02-22T21:39:29Z

### Steps to reproduce

Hoping to get some guidance on making a consistent reproducible example. The error I'm observing (`No Failure App provided`) is occurring during `bin/rails test` and originates in the [warden gem](https://github.com/wardencommunity/warden/blob/67f5ba6baaa7564ec79afef02cf3a4d0f7d312e5/lib/warden/manager.rb#L145). This only occurs about 20% of the time, i.e., running `bin/rails test` will complete without errors 4/5 times. The error only occurs when using the `with_routing` helper, e.g., 

```ruby
class ErrorPagesConcernTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  with_routing do |routes|
    routes.draw do
      %w[action_not_found invalid_authenticity_token name_error no_method_error record_not_found routing_error standard_error].each do |action|
        get "/default/#{action}", to: "error_pages_test##{action}"
        get "/rescued/#{action}", to: "rescued_error_pages_test##{action}"
      end
    end
  end
  
  ...
end
```

However, when I remove the `with_routing` helper and put the testing routes directly in `routes.rb`, the test suite runs without error 100% of the time.

### Expected behavior

The results of a test suit should be consistent when using the `with_routing` helper.

### Actual behavior

Using the `with_routing` helper causes inconsistent results in tests.

### System configuration

**Rails version**: 8.0.1

**Ruby version**: 3.2.6

@Edouard-chin, thanks for the guidance! I found that my tests still failed consistently (`PARALLEL_WORKERS=1 bin/rails test --seed 29227`) using the `main` branch of devise, but it got me on the right track. After adding `Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)` to my test:

```ruby
class ErrorPagesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)

  with_routing do |routes|
  ...

```ruby
module ActionDispatch::Assertions::RoutingAssertions::WithIntegrationRouting::ClassMethods
  def with_routing(&block)
    Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)
    # .. existing code left unchanged
  end
end
```

@Edouard-chin, thanks for the guidance! I found that my tests still failed consistently (`PARALLEL_WORKERS=1 bin/rails test --seed 29227`) using the `main` branch of devise, but it got me on the right track. After adding `Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)` to my test:

```ruby
class ErrorPagesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)

  with_routing do |routes|
  ...
  end

  ...
end
```

my test suite passes consistently again. I found that I had to call `reload_routes_unless_loaded` before `with_routing` to get it to work. Putting it inside the `with_routing` block had no effect. I also verified that the following "patch" worked:

```ruby
module ActionDispatch::Assertions::RoutingAssertions::WithIntegrationRouting::ClassMethods
  def with_routing(&block)
    Rails.application.try(:reload_routes_unless_loaded)
    # .. existing code left unchanged
  end
end
```

Would it make sense to open a PR with this change? Would all the `with_routing` methods (I count 4) require this addition?

Thanks for digging on this. Glad that you found a temporary solution.

> Would it make sense to open a PR with this change? 

Don't take my words for granted as I haven't looked, but I don't think so.
The `with_routing` is supposed to create a temporary route set (which doesn't use the lazy load feature), so reloading the previous route set that aren't going to be used should have no influence. Though I understand it fixes your issue somehow, I suspect the issue would need to be fixed on devise rather than Rails.

Now that we have scoped down the issue, maybe you can try creating a reproduction script without devise and see if the issue is really in Rails' `with_routing` method.

title: PG::SyntaxError for queries after upgrade from 7.1.5.1 to 7.2.2.1
need_summary: The developer needed a workaround for PostgreSQL's inability to use positional parameters with the timestamp typecast in Rails 7.2.2.1, and the answer provided a concrete fix using ':time::timestamp' with reference to commit 8e6a5deca626c944933211d7977f4e7e76869e74.
security_topic: PostgreSQL bind parameter casting limitation causing syntax error after Rails upgrade
question_text:
Error is raised
```
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: PG::SyntaxError: ERROR:  syntax error at or near "$2"
LINE 1: ...("availabilities"."state" IN ($1)) AND (timestamp $2 <@ avai...
```
answer_text:
I think this is going to be hard to fix on our side. This is due to a limitation on postgres server where you can't use a positional parameter and this typecast syntax:

```sql
prepare testquery2 (timestamp) AS SELECT timestamp '$1'; # Syntax problem
```

It used to work before because Active Record was interpolating the value in the query, but this changed in 8e6a5deca626c944933211d7977f4e7e76869e74 to instead build a query with bind parameters.

To solve your issue I'd recommend using a different postgres syntax for casting which works with parameters:

```sql
prepare testquery2 (timestamp) AS SELECT $1::timestamp
```

In your case:
```ruby
scope :currently_live, lambda { |time|
  active.where(':time::timestamp <@ availabilities.timespan', time: time)
}
```

title: Incorrect concurrent Postgres type map lookups by Hstore OID with multiple shards
need_summary: The needed security‑related fix for the concurrent type‑map bug is provided by PR #54510 (https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54510) which backports the correction.
security_topic: backporting fix for race condition causing deserialization errors
question_text: it would be great if https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c or [an alternative fix ](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54502#issuecomment-2653376233)could be backported to 7.2 and 8.0.
answer_text: If a more targeted fix is prefered for the backport, I think https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54510 does the trick.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54502: Incorrect concurrent Postgres type map lookups by Hstore OID with multiple shards
Author: joshuay03
Date: 2025-02-12T07:38:23Z
Labels: activerecord, attached PR, PostgreSQL
State: open

[c0]
We ran into this at @buildkite when upgrading to 7.2.2.1.

This seems to have been introduced in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa which was first included in 7.2, and happens to be fixed by https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c which is currently only on main.

I think the issue is that before https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa when defining attributes, [type lookups using the column (and therefore oid)](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-eee8446909a6221877323c7b605b430eaf515d8e66aa27ae62de2e7614014c95L619-L629) only occurred inside `load_schema!`, [right after schema load](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-eee8446909a6221877323c7b605b430eaf515d8e66aa27ae62de2e7614014c95R604-R606), and always with a mutex held by the caller (`load_schema`). After that change, [these lookups happen inside `_default_attributes`](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-2a6a5a31a6210a1e7036784fb31c738e1d2874bb5ae123d03737db02cb198876R242-R244), and it seems the schema may be re-loaded by another thread between column retrieval and lookup.

~What I don't yet understand is that the schema cache and type map seem to be per-connection/shard, and the lookup checks its own connection out of the pool, so the oid used for the lookup and the oid in the type map should be the same. But in my debugging I found that the lookup oid would be for a different connection/shard to the one already in the type map.~ Okay I think I got it. I thought [the `columns_hash` lookup](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9621e5989de6dd7d599c6af10fa7f65bcaf1e267/activerecord/lib/active_record/attributes.rb#L246) was hitting the schema cache, but it's not, it's just [stored on the class](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9621e5989de6dd7d599c6af10fa7f65bcaf1e267/activerecord/lib/active_record/model_schema.rb#L427-L430), which means a connection to another shard could have set it. Before, `@columns_hash` was set from the schema cache results and then its columns used for the lookup synchronously. Now, there may be a race condition between when the current thread sets it, and reads it, as another thread may have set it in-between when loading schema using another connection.

https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c then happens to fix this by removing the lookup altogether and storing the cast type on the column itself during schema load.

cc/ @jonathanhefner @rafaelfranca Sorry for the tags, but it would be great if https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c or [an alternative fix ](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54502#issuecomment-2653376233)could be backported to 7.2 and 8.0. This was a bit of a nasty bug to run into in production as it resulted in some invalid data persisting due to incorrect deserialization, and was not straightforward to debug.

### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  # gem "rails", path: "./"
  # gem "rails", "7.1.5.1" # ✅
  gem "rails", "7.2.2.1" # ❌
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "7-2-stable" # ❌
  # gem "rails", "8.0.1" # ❌
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "8-0-stable" # ❌
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main" # ✅

  gem "pg", "~> 1.1"
end

require "active_record/railtie"
require "minitest/autorun"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f
  config.eager_load = true
  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

  config.active_record.encryption.primary_key = "primary_key"
  config.active_record.encryption.deterministic_key = "deterministic_key"
  config.active_record.encryption.key_derivation_salt = "key_derivation_salt"
end
Rails.application.initialize!

# Note: This script pairs with a config/database.yml that has the following:
#
# development:
#   primary:
#     adapter: postgresql
#     database: development_primary
#   shard_001:
#     adapter: postgresql
#     database: development_shard_001
#   shard_002:
#     adapter: postgresql
#     database: development_shard_002
#
# and Postgres databases named `development_primary`, `development_shard_001`,
# and `development_shard_002`, each with the hstore extension enabled.

class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class

  connects_to database: { writing: :primary, reading: :primary }
end

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.hstore :metadata
  end
end

class ShardRecord < ApplicationRecord
  self.abstract_class = true

  connects_to shards: {
    shard_001: { writing: :shard_001, reading: :shard_001 },
    shard_002: { writing: :shard_002, reading: :shard_002 }
  }
end

[:shard_001, :shard_002].each do |shard|
  ShardRecord.connected_to(shard: shard) do
    ShardRecord.connection.create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
      t.hstore :metadata
    end
  end
end

class Post < ShardRecord
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_association_stuff
    25.times.map do |i|
      Thread.new do
        [:shard_001, :shard_002].sample.tap do |shard|
          ShardRecord.connected_to(shard: shard) do
            Post.create!(metadata: {}) # raises `TypeError: can't cast Hash`
          end
        end
      end
    end.each(&:join)
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->

All post records should be created successfully.

### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->

`TypeError: can't cast Hash` is raised, full stack trace on 7.2.2.1:

```
  1) Error:
BugTest#test_association_stuff:
TypeError: can't cast Hash
    activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/quoting.rb:105:in 'ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::Quoting#type_cast'
    activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/postgresql/quoting.rb:185:in 'ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQL::Quoting#type_cast'

comments.body:
We ran into this at @buildkite when upgrading to 7.2.2.1.

This seems to have been introduced in https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa which was first included in 7.2, and happens to be fixed by https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c which is currently only on main.

I think the issue is that before https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa when defining attributes, [type lookups using the column (and therefore oid)](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-eee8446909a6221877323c7b605b430eaf515d8e66aa27ae62de2e7614014c95L619-L629) only occurred inside `load_schema!`, [right after schema load](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-eee8446909a6221877323c7b605b430eaf515d8e66aa27ae62de2e7614014c95R604-R606), and always with a mutex held by the caller (`load_schema`). After that change, [these lookups happen inside `_default_attributes`](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/e0a55b038f7f2f50d1467876558be183be6cedaa#diff-2a6a5a31a6210a1e7036784fb31c738e1d2874bb5ae123d03737db02cb198876R242-R244), and it seems the schema may be re-loaded by another thread between column retrieval and lookup.

~What I don't yet understand is that the schema cache and type map seem to be per-connection/shard, and the lookup checks its own connection out of the pool, so the oid used for the lookup and the oid in the type map should be the same. But in my debugging I found that the lookup oid would be for a different connection/shard to the one already in the type map.~ Okay I think I got it. I thought [the `columns_hash` lookup](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9621e5989de6dd7d599c6af10fa7f65bcaf1e267/activerecord/lib/active_record/attributes.rb#L246) was hitting the schema cache, but it's not, it's just [stored on the class](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9621e5989de6dd7d599c6af10fa7f65bcaf1e267/activerecord/lib/active_record/model_schema.rb#L427-L430), which means a connection to another shard could have set it. Before, `@columns_hash` was set from the schema cache results and then its columns used for the lookup synchronously. Now, there may be a race condition between when the current thread sets it, and reads it, as another thread may have set it in-between when loading schema using another connection.

https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c then happens to fix this by removing the lookup altogether and storing the cast type on the column itself during schema load.

cc/ @jonathanhefner @rafaelfranca Sorry for the tags, but it would be great if https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/9ad36e067222478090b36a985090475bb03e398c or [an alternative fix ](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54502#issuecomment-2653376233)could be backported to 7.2 and 8.0. This was a bit of a nasty bug to run into in production as it resulted in some invalid data persisting due to incorrect deserialization, and was not straightforward to debug.

title: ActiveStorage creates conflicting checksums when using S3-compatible services on Blob.create_and_upload!
need_summary: How to configure ActiveStorage’s S3 service to send only a single checksum for S3‑compatible storage, answered with the concrete configuration flags request_checksum_calculation:"when_required" and response_checksum_validation:"when_required" (and specific aws-sdk-s3 gem versions) as the anchor.
security_topic: checksum conflict with S3-compatible storage in ActiveStorage
question_text: ActiveStorage creates conflicting checksums when using S3-compatible services on Blob.create_and_upload!
answer_text:
Activestorage already forwards options to the underlying service (s3 in our case)

So all that is needed is to add cloudflare's recommended options

Which gives us:
```yaml
# Use bin/rails credentials:edit to set the AWS secrets (as aws:access_key_id|secret_access_key)
amazon:
  service: S3
  access_key_id: <%= Rails.application.credentials.dig(:aws, :access_key_id) %>
  secret_access_key: <%= Rails.application.credentials.dig(:aws, :secret_access_key) %>
  region: "" # e.g. 'us-east-1'
  bucket: your_own_bucket-<%= Rails.env %>
  http_open_timeout: 0
  http_read_timeout: 0
  retry_limit: 0
  request_checksum_calculation: "when_required"
  response_checksum_validation: "when_required"
```
thread_text:
ISSUE #54374: ActiveStorage creates conflicting checksums when using S3-compatible services on Blob.create_and_upload!
Author: richjdsmith
Date: 2025-01-27T18:55:59Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]


## Description
When using ActiveStorage with S3-compatible services (specifically Cloudflare R2), `ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!` fails because it sends two different checksums to the storage service. While Amazon S3 accepts multiple checksums, other S3-compatible services may not support this behavior.

## Environment
- Rails version: 8.0.1
- Ruby version: 3.3.6
- AWS SDK S3 gem version: 1.178.0
- Storage service: Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure ActiveStorage to use an S3-compatible service:
```yaml
# config/storage.yml
cloudflare:
  service: S3
  endpoint: https://account_id.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
  access_key_id: access_key
  secret_access_key: secret_key
  region: auto
  bucket: bucket_name
```

2. Attempt to upload a file using `create_and_upload!`:
```ruby
blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
  io: params[:file],
  filename: params[:file].original_filename,
  content_type: params[:file].content_type
)
```

## Current Behavior
The upload fails with:
```
Aws::S3::Errors::InvalidRequest You can only specify one checksum at a time.
```

Debug logs show that two checksums are being sent:
```ruby
put_object(
  body: #<ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile...>,
  content_md5: "ggvRot1GXgDw4lbwRpD6eQ==",    # First checksum from ActiveStorage
  content_type: "image/jpeg",
  content_disposition: nil,
  metadata: {},
  bucket: "bucket_name",
  key: "key123",
  checksum_algorithm: "CRC32"                  # Second checksum from AWS SDK
)
```

## Expected Behavior
ActiveStorage should either:
1. Allow configuration of checksum behavior for S3-compatible services
2. Only send one type of checksum
3. Detect S3-compatible services and adjust behavior accordingly

## Workaround
The issue can be worked around by manually creating the blob with the checksum in advance:

```ruby
service = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
key = SecureRandom.base58(24)
 # Calculate checksum manually, in advance
checksum = Digest::MD5.file(params[:image].tempfile).base64digest

blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create!(
  key: key,
  filename: file.original_filename,
  byte_size: file.size,
  checksum: checksum,  # Prevent ActiveStorage from adding MD5
  content_type: file.content_type,
  service_name: service.name
)

service.upload(
  key, 
  file,
  content_type: file.content_type
)
```

This allows the AWS SDK to handle checksums with just CRC32, which works with S3-compatible services.

## Additional Notes
- Regular file uploads through forms work fine (they use a different code path)
- Direct uploads through ActiveStorage's built-in controller also work
- The issue specifically occurs with `create_and_upload!`
- This affects any S3-compatible service that doesn't support multiple checksums

comments.author: richjdsmith
comments.body:
## Description
When using ActiveStorage with S3-compatible services (specifically Cloudflare R2), `ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!` fails because it sends two different checksums to the storage service. While Amazon S3 accepts multiple checksums, other S3-compatible services may not support this behavior.

## Environment
- Rails version: 8.0.1
- Ruby version: 3.3.6
- AWS SDK S3 gem version: 1.178.0
- Storage service: Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure ActiveStorage to use an S3-compatible service:
```yaml
# config/storage.yml
cloudflare:
  service: S3
  endpoint: https://account_id.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
  access_key_id: access_key
  secret_access_key: secret_key
  region: auto
  bucket: bucket_name
```

2. Attempt to upload a file using `create_and_upload!`:
```ruby
blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(
  io: params[:file],
  filename: params[:file].original_filename,
  content_type: params[:file].content_type
)
```

## Current Behavior
The upload fails with:
```
Aws::S3::Errors::InvalidRequest You can only specify one checksum at a time.
```

Debug logs show that two checksums are being sent:
```ruby
put_object(
  body: #<ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile...>,
  content_md5: "ggvRot1GXgDw4lbwRpD6eQ==",    # First checksum from ActiveStorage
  content_type: "image/jpeg",
  content_disposition: nil,
  metadata: {},
  bucket: "bucket_name",
  key: "key123",
  checksum_algorithm: "CRC32"                  # Second checksum from AWS SDK
)
```

## Expected Behavior
ActiveStorage should either:
1. Allow configuration of checksum behavior for S3-compatible services
2. Only send one type of checksum
3. Detect S3-compatible services and adjust behavior accordingly

## Workaround
The issue can be worked around by manually creating the blob with the checksum in advance:

```ruby
service = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
key = SecureRandom.base58(24)
 # Calculate checksum manually, in advance
checksum = Digest::MD5.file(params[:image].tempfile).base64digest

blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create!(
  key: key,
  filename: file.original_filename,
  byte_size: file.size,
  checksum: checksum,  # Prevent ActiveStorage from adding MD5
  content_type: file.content_type,
  service_name: service.name
)

service.upload(
  key, 
  file,
  content_type: file.content_type
)
```

This allows the AWS SDK to handle checksums with just CRC32, which works with S3-compatible services.

## Additional Notes
- Regular file uploads through forms work fine (they use a different code path)
- Direct uploads through ActiveStorage's built-in controller also work
- The issue specifically occurs with `create_and_upload!`
- This affects any S3-compatible service that doesn't support multiple checksums

## Suggested Fix
Consider adding a configuration option in ActiveStorage's S3 service to specify checksum behavior:

```yaml
cloudflare:
  service: S3
  # ...other configs...
  checksum_mode: single  # or 'multiple' for regular S3
```

Or detect S3-compatible services based on the endpoint and adjust behavior automatically.

comments.author: AliSepehri
comments.body:
`on_rotation` is supported by `MessageVerifier`, but the Signed Id implementation does not pass it through. This feature is very useful for secret-key rotation and monitoring the usage of old keys.

### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails"
  gem "sqlite3"
end

require "active_record/railtie"
require "minitest/autorun"

ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = "sqlite3::memory:"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f
  config.eager_load = false
  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

  ActiveRecord::Base.signed_id_verifier_secret = "new_secret"
end
Rails.application.initialize!

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_association_stuff
    Post.create! id: 1

    on_rotation_is_called = false

    # signed Id of "1" with "old_secret"
    signed_id_with_old_secret = "eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MSwicHVyIjoicG9zdCJ9fQ--e3c0118ae573077a32264dc32acc63800352323c41039b0e096af64bd6ecc28b"

    Post.signed_id_verifier.rotate "old_secret", on_rotation: -> { on_rotation_is_called = true }
    assert Post.find_signed!(signed_id_with_old_secret, on_rotation: -> { on_rotation_is_called = true })

    assert on_rotation_is_called
  end
end
```

### Expected Behavior
`on_rotation` should be called, and `on_rotation_is_called` should become true.

### Actual Behavior
The `on_rotation` method from `rotate` or `find_signed!` is not called, leaving `on_rotation_is_called` as false.

### Suggestions
1. Call `on_rotation` when it is set using the `rotate` method. This would require updating the `read_message` method in `activesupport/lib/active_support/messages/rotator.rb` file.

2. Call `on_rotation` when it is set using `find_signed`/`find_signed!`. These methods would need to accept `on_rotation` as an optional argument.

3. Implement both solutions.

title: PoolConfig caches the connection_class, which breaks if it is reloaded
need_summary: The developer needed to know how to prevent caching the connection class in PoolConfig to keep write‑prevention checks reliable, which is addressed by the concrete fix in commit e901ce1c that stores the class name and primary flag instead of the class object.
security_topic: incorrect write-prevention due to cached connection class after reload
question_text: @eileencodes any idea on how to fix this problem?
answer_text:
Would it be acceptable to cache the name and its primary-ness, rather than caching the class?

```patch
commit e901ce1c (HEAD -> flavorjones-dont-cache-class-in-pool-config)
Author: Mike Dalessio <mike.dalessio@gmail.com>
Date:   2025-01-24 14:32:09 -0500

    Avoid caching the connection class in the PoolConfig
    
    Instead, cache the name and whether it's primary.

diff --git a/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/pool_config.rb b/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/pool_config.rb
index 0010a48a..1a3ad417 100644
--- a/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/pool_config.rb
+++ b/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/pool_config.rb
@@ -7,7 +7,6 @@ class PoolConfig # :nodoc:
 
        attr_reader :db_config, :role, :shard
        attr_writer :schema_reflection, :server_version
-       attr_accessor :connection_class
 
        def schema_reflection
          @schema_reflection ||= SchemaReflection.new(db_config.lazy_schema_cache_path)
@@ -29,7 +28,7 @@ def disconnect_all!
        def initialize(connection_class, db_config, role, shard)
          super()
          @server_version = nil
-         @connection_class = connection_class
+         self.connection_class = connection_class
          @db_config = db_config
          @role = role
          @shard = shard
@@ -41,11 +40,20 @@ def server_version(connection)
          @server_version || synchronize { @server_version ||= connection.get_database_version }
        end
 
+       def connection_class=(connection_class)
+         @connection_class_name = connection_class.name
+         @connection_class_primary_p = connection_class.primary_class?
+       end
+
+       def connection_class
+         @connection_class_name.constantize
+       end
+
        def connection_name
-         if connection_class.primary_class?
+         if @connection_class_primary_p
            "ActiveRecord::Base"
          else
-         connection_class.name
+         @connection_class_name
          end
        end
``` 

The downside, I guess, is doing unnecessary `constantize` in production code.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54343: PoolConfig caches the connection_class, which breaks if it is reloaded
Author: djmb
Date: 2025-01-24T14:44:52Z
Labels: activerecord, pinned
State: closed

[c0]
I've been debugging [this Solid Cache issue](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache/issues/238), and it looks like it is caused by reloading the connection class.

It is [stored](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/31f8a6b6cce5e38f1f8a9532d441c4d19ca8fb08/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/pool_config.rb#L32) in the `ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PoolConfig`, and if the connection class is reloaded, then 
it no longer matches the stored value.

This breaks checks like [this](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/31f8a6b6cce5e38f1f8a9532d441c4d19ca8fb08/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb#L198), leading to issues like the one we see in the Solid Cache bug.

You can reproduce in a development console if you are using Solid Cache like this:

```ruby
>> ActiveRecord::Base.connected_to(role: ActiveRecord.reading_role, prevent_writes: true) do 
  SolidCache::Record.connected_to(shard: :cache, role: :writing, prevent_writes: false) do
     puts SolidCache::Record.connection.preventing_writes?
  end
end
false
=> nil
>> reload!

title: Rails no longer looks for `secret_key_base` in credentials (in development)
need_summary: The developer needed to know if the change in how Rails looks up secret_key_base impacts cookie security and which Rails version restores the previous precedence, which is answered by noting that Rails 7.2 (7.2.2.1) re‑establishes tmp/local_secret.txt taking precedence over credentials
security_topic: development secret_key_base precedence
question_text: How can we bring back credentials lookup for `secret_key_base` in development (instead of the generated secret file)?
answer_text: I've now moved my upgrading process to Rails 7.2 and can confirm as of 7.2.2.1 (probably earlier) the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file takes precedence over the `secret_key_base` in `config/credentials.yml.enc` again.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54277: Rails no longer looks for `secret_key_base` in credentials (in development)
Author: maxim
Date: 2025-01-17T06:36:15Z
Labels: railties, pinned
State: closed

[c0]
Rails 7.1 automatically found `secret_key_base` in credentials when in development env.

Rails 7.2 doesn't look there anymore, when in development env. It now always generates a secret file and uses that.

It seems the only way to bring back credentials lookup in development is by setting it manually in development.rb:

```ruby
config.secret_key_base = credentials[:secret_key_base]
```

This change is not mentioned in Rails 7.1 -> 7.2 upgrade guide, so it was quite unsettling to find out that all my cookies stopped working after the update. (Since Rails silently switched to using the generated key over the key in my credentials file).

Here's the [relevant code](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/4666f596861a2d53ff0d7fb055206355b5a13de2/railties/lib/rails/application/configuration.rb#L511).

Whether the solution might be to document this in the upgrade guide, or make Rails honor the key stored in credentials, it seems to be an issue worth addressing.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @brendon 2025-02-13T06:48:58Z:
Here's what I've noticed too:

With Rails 6.1 and 7.0 in development, the `secret_key_base` is read from `tmp/development_secret.txt` as a preference over the production `secret_key_base` defined via `rails credentials:edit`. This is reversed in the latest Rails 7.1 so now it uses the production `secret_key_base` defined via `rails credentials:edit` instead of what's in `tmp/local_secret.txt`.

I've confirmed this by loading the key from the text file into the credentials and all of the ActionText attachments work again.
---
[c2] @brendon 2025-02-13T22:15:43Z:
I've now moved my upgrading process to Rails 7.2 and can conform as of 7.2.2.1 (probably earlier) the `tmp/local_secret.txt` file takes precedence over the `secret_key_base` in `config/credentials.yml.enc` again.

Perhaps there should be a backport of this behaviour to Rails 7.1 to prevent people wasting time trying to sort it out?
---

title: `./bin/rails assets:precompile` is loading ActiveStorage s3 configuration after upgrading from Rails 7.1 -> 7.2 or 8.0
need_summary: The issue was caused by commit 8bf1353cae which loads ActiveStorage::Blob during boot, causing assets:precompile to load S3 credentials and potentially expose them; fixing or awaiting the patch resolves the problem.
security_topic: unexpected loading of ActiveStorage configuration during asset precompilation
question_text: I would expect to be able to run `RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 ./bin/rails assets:precompile` and not have any dependency on ActiveStorage/devise. Commenting out `devise_for` from routes.rb or the `has_one_attached` from the User model resolves the problem.
answer_text: It seems it was caused by 8bf1353cae. If I got it right, that code is now loading `ActiveStorage::Blob` during boot time.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54139: `./bin/rails assets:precompile` is loading ActiveStorage s3 configuration after upgrading from Rails 7.1 -> 7.2 or 8.0
Author: michaelroudnitski
Date: 2025-01-07T16:38:32Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
## Current behavior

Hi, I hope this is the right place to report this.

I spent some time debugging an error I encountered after starting my Rails 7.1 -> 8.0 upgrade.

I was able to reproduce it with a new rails 8 app, installing devise and configuring ActiveStorage to use S3. It seems like when you run `RAILS_ENV=production rails assets:precompile`, it is now loading ActiveStorage attachments on the User model from the devise routes.rb entrypoint, which is undesired.

This was not the case on Rails 7.1 and seems to be reproducable after upgrading to Rails 7.2. I was not able to find anything obvious from the [ActiveStorage 7.2 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activestorage/CHANGELOG.md#rails-720-august-09-2024). I would guess something changed with autoloading that causes routes.rb to get picked up and evaluated during the precompile task?

  devise :database_authenticatable, :registerable,
         :recoverable, :rememberable, :validatable

## Current behavior

Hi, I hope this is the right place to report this.

I spent some time debugging an error I encountered after starting my Rails 7.1 -> 8.0 upgrade.

I was able to reproduce it with a new rails 8 app, installing devise and configuring ActiveStorage to use S3. It seems like when you run `RAILS_ENV=production rails assets:precompile`, it is now loading ActiveStorage attachments on the User model from the devise routes.rb entrypoint, which is undesired.

This was not the case on Rails 7.1 and seems to be reproducable after upgrading to Rails 7.2. I was not able to find anything obvious from the [ActiveStorage 7.2 changelog](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activestorage/CHANGELOG.md#rails-720-august-09-2024). I would guess something changed with autoloading that causes routes.rb to get picked up and evaluated during the precompile task?

### To reproduce:

1. create a new rails 8 app
2. run `bundle add devise` and setup devise as normal on a User model
3. add an attachment to the User model
```ruby
# app/models/user.rb
class User < ApplicationRecord
  # Include default devise modules. Others available are:
  # :confirmable, :lockable, :timeoutable, :trackable and :omniauthable
  devise :database_authenticatable, :registerable,
         :recoverable, :rememberable, :validatable
  has_one_attached :display_picture
end
```
4. configure ActiveStorage to use the S3 service in `production.rb`,
```ruby
# config/storage.yml
s3:
  service: S3
  public: true
  access_key_id: "123"
  secret_access_key: "123"
  endpoint: "https://s3.example.cloud"
  region: null # purposely set to null to mimic secrets not being available in a docker build stage
  bucket: "bucket"

# config/environments/production.rb
config.active_storage.service = :s3
```
5. run `RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 ./bin/rails assets:precompile --trace` and observe an error from our ActiveStorage setup not having a configuration set
```
RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 ./bin/rails assets:precompile --trace
** Invoke assets:precompile (first_time)
** Invoke environment (first_time)
** Execute environment
bin/rails aborted!
Aws::Errors::MissingRegionError: No region was provided. Configure the `:region` option or export the region name to ENV['AWS_REGION'] (Aws::Errors::MissingRegionError)

comments.author: rafaelfranca
comments.body:
`RAILS_ENV=production rails assets:precompile` always loaded all the application code, including routes and models. This wasn't the behavior that changed. You can check that in Rails 7.1 by raising on the top of the user model if you want.

I don't know why you didn't get that error on Rails 7.1, but you should.

Can you confirm adding `raise` on top of `user.rb` causes the application to also fail on Rails 7.1?

comments.author: michaelroudnitski
comments.body:
@rafaelfranca yes you're right, adding `raise` to the top of `user.rb` also causes it to fail on Rails 7.1.

worth noting: on rails 7.1 with `raise` at the top of the user model, removing `devise_for :users` from `routes.rb` results in `precompile` succeeding

> I don't know why you didn't get that error on Rails 7.1, but you should.

I thought it could be another gem I upgraded in the process, but even following my same reproduction steps for a new Rails 7.1 app `rails _7.1_ new 7_1-app`, running `assets:precompile` is successful

comments.body: Thanks for confirming. I guess now that you have a new app you could try to bisect to see which change broke this behavior. If you can share a repo with this new app I can try to do that.

comments.author: rafaelfranca
comments.body:
@Mth0158 that code will still trigger the issue. It is wrong. You can't load the Rails frameworks without the load hooks.

Change it to:

```ruby
module ActiveStorageValidations
  class Railtie < ::Rails::Railtie
    initializer 'active_storage_validations.extend_active_storage_blob' do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_blob) do
        include(ActiveStorageValidations::ASVBlobMetadatable)
      end
    end
  end
end
```

Hi,

As a workaround for version 7.2 (while a new release is not made), it is possible to make the adjustment below:

```rb
# config/environments/production.rb

Rails.application.configure do
  ...
  # Store uploaded files on the local file system (see config/storage.yml for options).
  config.active_storage.service = ENV.fetch("STORAGE_PROVIDER", :azure)
  ...
end
```

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile

RUN RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 STORAGE_PROVIDER=local bundle exec rails assets:clean && \
    RAILS_ENV=production SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 STORAGE_PROVIDER=local bundle exec rails assets:precompile
```

This way, assets compile will run using local storage, but will maintain the desired service in other cases.

* Note: Remember of replace `:azure` with the service you're already using.

title: Fix Invalid Parameter Error Handling: Raise More Specific Exception in POST Method
need_summary: The developer asked whether changing ActionDispatch::Request#POST to raise a more specific ParseError for malformed multipart requests is appropriate, and the maintainer answered that this would break the default exception app and referenced the Rails guide on config.exceptions_app (https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#config-exceptions-app) as the source.
security_topic: exception handling for invalid multipart request parameters in Rails
question_text: Does this change make sense within the Rails architecture? Would it be appropriate to propose a pull request to implement this change, improving the handling of invalid parameters?
answer_text:
👋 I think this issue would need to be fixed in your application. In a vanilla Rails app, the 400.html page is displayed correctly.

> `match "/400", to: "errors#bad_request", via: :all, as: "bad_request"`

I suppose if you have this route you also have set your `config.exceptions_app` to `Rails.application.routes`, right?

You'll need to wrap the exception app, and handle the exception's cause. There is an example in the Rails guide that is similar: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#config-exceptions-app

>  suggest modifying the ActionDispatch::Request#POST method to raise a more specific exception,

We can't for two reasons:

1) This won't fix your issue. The exception is basically raised twice, once on request, and second when Rails tries to call your exception app. No matter the exception if your exception app doesn't handle it you'll get the issue.
2) This will break all Rails applications making use of the default exception app, as we specifically rescue BadRequest to display the 400.html page.
thread_text:
ISSUE #54096: Fix Invalid Parameter Error Handling: Raise More Specific Exception in POST Method
Author: pozzer
Date: 2025-01-02T18:04:29Z
Labels: With reproduction steps
State: open

[c0]
### Steps to reproduce
To reproduce this issue, send a malicious or exploratory request targeting an endpoint configured to accept multipart uploads. For example, use the following curl command:

```bash
$ curl --request POST 'http://localhost:3000/any_path' \
  --header 'Content-Type:multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryxQm6bAVJJEu1FxWw' \
  --data '---invalid-boundary'
```
The Content-Type header specifies a boundary, but the request body contains invalid data, leading to the error.
  
### Expected behavior
The invalid request should be handled properly, and a 400 Bad Request error should be routed to the appropriate handler, such as:

```ruby 
match "/400", to: "errors#bad_request", via: :all, as: "bad_request"
```

### Actual behavior
The error is intercepted by the Rack middleware and forwarded to the Controller, but the exception raised `(ActionController::BadRequest: Invalid request parameters: Rack::Multipart::EmptyContentError) `occurs before it hits the controller cycle. The standard `rescue_from` mechanism does not catch the error, and the request does not reach the` /400` route handler.

### System configuration

**Rails version**: Rails 8.0.1
**Ruby version**: 3.3.5

### Steps to reproduce
The issue occurs in the `filtered_parameters` method in `ActionDispatch::Http::FilterParameters`, which is designed to handle parameter parsing errors:
```ruby
def filtered_parameters
  @filtered_parameters ||= parameter_filter.filter(parameters)
rescue ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError
  @filtered_parameters = {}
end
```
However, the error raised is an `ActionController::BadRequest`, originating from the `ActionDispatch::Request#POST` method:

```ruby
rescue ActionDispatch::ParamsParser::ParseError, EOFError => e
  raise ActionController::BadRequest.new("Invalid request parameters: #{e.message}")  
```
Because ActionController::BadRequest is not caught by filtered_parameters, the request flow is interrupted before it can reach the configured error handling route.

### Proposed Solution
I suggest modifying the `ActionDispatch::Request#POST` method to raise a more specific exception, such as `ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError`, instead of `ActionController::BadRequest`:
```ruby
raise ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError.new("Invalid request parameters: #{e.message}")
```
### Community Question

Does this change make sense within the Rails architecture? Would it be appropriate to propose a pull request to implement this change, improving the handling of invalid parameters?

Thank you for your attention and feedback!

comments.author: Edouard-chin
comments.body:
👋 I think this issue would need to be fixed in your application. In a vanilla Rails app, the 400.html page is displayed correctly.

> `match "/400", to: "errors#bad_request", via: :all, as: "bad_request"`

I suppose if you have this route you also have set your `config.exceptions_app` to `Rails.application.routes`, right?

You'll need to wrap the exception app, and handle the exception's cause. There is an example in the Rails guide that is similar: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#config-exceptions-app

>  suggest modifying the ActionDispatch::Request#POST method to raise a more specific exception,

We can't for two reasons:

1) This won't fix your issue. The exception is basically raised twice, once on request, and second when Rails tries to call your exception app. No matter the exception if your exception app doesn't handle it you'll get the issue.
2) This will break all Rails applications making use of the default exception app, as we specifically rescue BadRequest to display the 400.html page.
